feedback:
Written before this candidate races, so no outcome is claimed for it. The evidence is iteration 1 (score 134.06, the best so far) and the iteration 0 baseline (score 49.8). In iteration 1 the oval finished in 1 of 20 trials at a mean time of 1.65 s, so base_speed 1.4 is fast enough to finish. The s-bend and slalom ended off track in every trial, with 1.15 to 1.25 line-loss events per run. Line loss is the main failure.

The wider array (x = ±0.036 m, 16 mm footprints) and the kp rise to 3.5 address that failure directly, and I support both. The problem is base_speed. The candidate cuts it from 1.4 to 1.1, which goes against the advice in iteration 1's feedback. The 3 s limit needs roughly 1.5 m/s on average, and the only finish so far came at 1.4. Slowing to 1.1 risks losing the 500-point completion bonus even if line loss improves. The candidate also changes array, kp and speed together, so the next race cannot separate their effects.

Revise: restore base_speed to 1.4 and keep the wider array and kp 3.5 so that the array and gain effects can be read against the iteration 1 baseline. Keep kd at 0.4 and ki at 0.02, and keep mass, sensor y and line_loss unchanged. If the revised build still shows more than 0.8 line-loss events per run after the array change, the next step is kd or kp, not speed. If it stays on the line but progress stalls under 0.6 with no off-track exit, then speed is the limit and base_speed should rise in 0.1 steps from 1.4.
requested_changes: Set base_speed back to 1.4. Iteration 1 finished the oval at 1.65 s at this speed, and 1.1 risks failing the 3 s limit.

Keep the wider array (sensor x at ±0.036 m, sensor_size 0.016) and kp 3.5, and hold kd at 0.4 and ki at 0.02, so the array and gain effects can be read against iteration 1's 1.15 to 1.45 line-loss events per run.
If line_loss_events stay above 0.8 per run after this change, raise kd from 0.4 toward 0.5 or 0.6 before raising kp further, since iteration 1 steering_oscillation was already about 0.29 on the oval.
